text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Military documents on religious activism will be used as evidence in a court case on the possible closure of the Islamist Welfare Party.
- Prime Minister Mesut Yilmaz says religious schools will be turned into secular, republican ones, sparking chaotic scenes in parliament as Islamists protest.
- Opium poppy production is encouraged for the first time in 23 years, winning approval from farmers in western and central Anatolia.
- A tourism official says ancient statues at the summit of Nemrut mountain in southeast Turkey have been knocked down by Islamists who regard them as idolatrous.
- High demand for shares in Sabanci Holding prompts the issue of extra paper worth 4 trillion lira ($26.5 million).
- The new government plans to reshuffle bureaucrats in the foreign ministry, intelligence services and treasury.
- Telephone calls made by special force members reveal how the casino king Omer Lutfu Topal was killed.
- Wheat producers are not satisfied by record prices given by the former Islamist-led government as the grain board will only buy 20 percent of the whole harvest.
- Libyan leader Muammar Gaddafi threatens Turks involved in contracting business in Libya with expulsion.
- The private sector is on a successful path, undisrupted by the political chaos of recent months.
